skill.name: wrike-automation
skill.description: Automate Wrike tasks, folders, projects, assignments, blueprints, and workspace operations through the Rube MCP integration.
skill.summary: Manage common Wrike workflows through guided Rube MCP tool sequences.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The backtick and reconnaissance detections are false positives caused by Markdown formatting and ordinary Wrike documentation. Real risks remain from third-party OAuth delegation and irreversible deletion workflows that lack mandatory confirmation.

remediation.issue: Folder and space deletion can permanently remove broad sets of Wrike data without a required approval gate.
remediation.suggestion: Require the user to confirm the resolved resource name, identifier, and deletion scope immediately before every permanent deletion.

remediation.issue: Rube MCP receives delegated Wrike access through OAuth, creating an external trust boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Require users to verify the MCP endpoint and review requested OAuth permissions before authorizing the connection.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Wrike connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `wrike`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
2. `WRIKE_GET_ALL_CUSTOM_FIELDS` - Get custom field IDs if needed [Optional]
- `folderId`: Parent folder ID where the task will be created
- `responsibles`: Array of user IDs to assign
- `dates`: Object with type, start, due, duration
- `folderId`: Parent folder ID for creation; target folder ID for modification
- `customItemTypeId`: Set to create as a project instead of a folder
- `shareds`: Array of user IDs or emails to share with
- `project`: Filter for projects (true) or folders (false) in GET_FOLDERS
2. `WRIKE_GET_TASK_BY_ID` - Get detailed info for a specific task [Optional]
- `taskId`: Specific task ID for detailed retrieval
- `resolve_user_names`: Auto-resolve user IDs to names (default true)
2. `WRIKE_LIST_SPACE_TASK_BLUEPRINTS` - List blueprints in a specific space [Alternative]
- `task_blueprint_id`: ID of the blueprint to launch
3. `WRIKE_CREATE_INVITATION` - Invite a user to the workspace [Optional]
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Either parent_id or super_task_id is required, not both
- Custom email subjects/messages require a paid Wrike plan
2. Find field by name, extract id and type
| Launch blueprint | WRIKE_LAUNCH_TASK_BLUEPRINT_ASYNC | task_blueprint_id, title, parent_id |

content.value_statement: Manual Wrike updates can slow project coordination and create inconsistent records. This skill guides Rube MCP tools for structured task, project, and workspace operations.
actual_capabilities: Creates and updates Wrike tasks with assignments, dates, importance, status, and custom fields.
Lists, creates, modifies, and deletes Wrike folders and projects.
Retrieves tasks by filters or identifiers and resolves assigned user names.
Lists and launches task blueprints with scheduling and parent controls.
Retrieves workspace contacts, creates invitations, and reads or deletes spaces.
Explains Wrike identifier resolution, pagination, permissions, and date formats.
limitations: Requires an active Rube MCP connection and completed Wrike OAuth authorization.
Available fields and operations depend on the connected Wrike plan and user permissions.
Task and folder searches may require pagination for complete results.
Deletion operations are irreversible and require careful human review.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Team Tasks
use_cases.description: Create assigned tasks with dates, status, importance, and custom fields inside the correct Wrike project.

use_cases.title: Monitor Delivery Progress
use_cases.description: Retrieve active or overdue tasks, resolve assignee names, and summarize current work across selected folders.

use_cases.title: Standardize Repeated Projects
use_cases.description: Find a task blueprint and launch a rescheduled copy in the required folder or parent task.

prompt_templates.title: List Active Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: List active Wrike tasks in [folder or project]. Include title, assignee, start date, due date, and status.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review current work in one project.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Assigned Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Wrike task named [title] in [project]. Assign [people], set dates to [dates], and show the resolved destination before creation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Add a clearly scoped task for a team.

prompt_templates.title: Launch a Project Blueprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the Wrike blueprint named [name]. Launch it under [project] with title [title] and reschedule its start to [date].
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a repeatable project from an approved template.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Update Overdue Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Find overdue active tasks in [scope]. Group them by assignee, propose status or date changes, and request approval before applying updates.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review multiple records before controlled bulk changes.

output_examples.input: List active tasks due this week in the Website Launch project.
output: Found 8 active tasks due this week in Website Launch.
Three tasks are due within two days, and two tasks have no assignee.
Results include task title, assignee, start date, due date, and status.

output_examples.input: Create a high-priority design review task for Maya due Friday.
output_examples.output: Created Design review in the approved project, assigned it to Maya, set high importance, and scheduled the requested due date.

output_examples.input: Delete the obsolete Campaign Archive folder.
output_examples.output: Campaign Archive contains 14 tasks and 3 subfolders. Permanent deletion is pending explicit confirmation for the resolved folder identifier.

best_practices: Search current tool schemas before each workflow because MCP tool parameters can change.
Resolve folders, users, custom fields, and blueprints by lookup instead of guessing identifiers.
Confirm resolved resources and impact before invitations, bulk updates, blueprint launches, or deletions.
anti_patterns: Do not guess Wrike identifiers from names or reuse identifiers from another workspace.
Do not delete folders or spaces without reviewing their contents and obtaining explicit approval.
Do not assume all records were returned when a tool response includes pagination.

faq.question: What connection does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires Rube MCP configured at the documented endpoint and an active Wrike OAuth connection.

faq.question: Can it assign tasks using a person name?
faq.answer: It must first resolve the person to a Wrike user identifier, then use that identifier for assignment.

faq.question: Can it manage custom fields?
faq.answer: Yes. It can retrieve custom field definitions and provide correctly structured values when creating or updating tasks.

faq.question: Does it support task blueprints?
faq.answer: Yes. It can list available blueprints and launch one under a folder, project, or parent task.

faq.question: Are deletion operations reversible?
faq.answer: Folder and space deletion are documented as permanent. Confirm the exact resource and impact before execution.

faq.question: Will every Wrike account support all operations?
faq.answer: No. Features depend on the connected user's permissions, workspace settings, and Wrike plan.
